I can’t diagnose health conditions or infer disability status from calendar titles. Those are sensitive attributes and the titles provide no reliable medical information — making employment decisions on that basis risks errors and unlawful discrimination.

What you can do instead (practical, lawful steps)
- Do not change duties or take adverse action based on assumptions.  
- Privately check in with the employee and invite them to share any needs or limitations. Keep the conversation supportive and confidential.  
- If the employee requests accommodations or you have a legitimate reason to seek verification, involve HR and follow your organization’s accommodation policy (and applicable laws such as the ADA in the U.S.). Request medical documentation only when appropriate and consistent with policy.  
- Conduct an individualized assessment: identify essential job functions, discuss possible accommodations, evaluate reasonableness and undue hardship, document the process and decisions.  
- If there are immediate safety or performance concerns unrelated to health, address those with objective evidence and standard performance-management steps, while still protecting privacy.

Sample neutral check-in message you can send
Hi [Name], I wanted to check in briefly — I saw appointments on your calendar this week and wanted to make sure you have any support or accommodations you might need. Can we schedule a private meeting to discuss? Anything you share will be treated confidentially. Thanks, [Your name]

If you’d like, I can:
- Draft a short private message or meeting script tailored to your workplace tone.  
- Outline a step-by-step accommodation intake checklist for HR/manager use.  
- Summarize best practices for documenting an interactive accommodation process.

Which would help you most?
